newsitem.title: USA: TCI to cut workforce by 6.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: TCI to cut workforce by 6.5 pct.

text.p: Tele-Communications Inc said on Thursday that it would cut its workforce by 6.5 percent and review all expenses not directly related to serving customers.
The company said it was making the reduction in an effort to strengthen its financial performance, improve its competitiveness and reduce debt.
The nation's largest cable television operator said it would lay off a total of about 2,500 managers and other employees from its corporate headquarters and field offices.
The planned reduction is larger than industry observers had expected, with analysts looking for TCI to cut about five percent of its workforce.
In a brief announcement, TCI said it would also implement salary reductions and pay freezes for senior executives unless the company met its business objectives.
The announcement follows a meeting this week between John Malone, TCI's chief executive, and a group of investors at the company's headquarters in Englewood.
TCI faces daunting challenges, including stiff competition from direct broadcast satellite (DBS) television services whose popularity has grown faster than experts had expected.
TCI shares have recently lingered near their 52-week low of 11-1/4, but rose as much as 5/8 on Thursday to 13-3/4.
